clue.text: Farmer traditionally associated with 25 and 23 7, initially 23

definitions.meaning: the name comes from the Greek georgos, a tiller of the soil, so by tradition it means a farmer
25 is HARRIS and 23 7 with only the initial of 7 is Jerome K. Jerome: the three men in Three Men in a Boat were J, Harris and this companion

explanation.walkthrough: '23 7, initially 23' is Araucaria's trick: JEROME, then K (the initial of KERN), then JEROME again gives Jerome K. Jerome, author of Three Men in a Boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Etymologically the name means earth-worker, and it is also the third man rowing with Harris and J in Jerome's comic novel.

clue.text: Ambiguous article removed with birds by 21 3 25

definitions.note: a phrase for a book or character created by the named writer

indicators.note: removed says the article is to be taken out of the word before it

parts.note: something ambiguous is unclear
A is the indefinite article
emus are large flightless birds

explanation.surface: Someone strips an unclear grammatical article and adds birds, all credited to an American author.
explanation.walkthrough: The unclear article is the A taken from UNCLEAR, leaving UNCLER, then EMUS. 21 3 25 is Joel Chandler Harris, who wrote the Uncle Remus stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Joel Chandler Harris created the old storyteller narrator of his Brer Rabbit tales, so that figure is one by him.

clue.text: See 21
Good catch at cover

to net a fish is to catch it

explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a fielding position in cricket, which is the surface picture; here it is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonnet is a head covering, so the word is an example of a cover.

clue.text: Water softener for the copper, pointless when child's about

explanation.definitionFit: A bath cube is a scented block dissolved in bathwater, sold as a softener for hard water.

clue.text: Little room on Tyneside for saint of Artois (I've just got there)

the WC, water closet, is the smallest room in the house

explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle in north-east England. The definition is what a newcomer might say.

clue.text: Nuns, sick having eaten fish, remaining calm

clue.text: On the way to 15 without fighting

explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'free of' but means outside. 15 is Brer Fox; the fox stands in for its dialect name.

clue.text: Dawdling with tart by lake

explanation.definitionFit: Flânerie is the French-derived word for aimless strolling, idle wandering about town.

clue.text: Many lousy places, let or otherwise, will affect the blood

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, standing for many
holes are slang for squalid, lousy places

explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges LETOR into TEROL. The definition is a description: the answer is something that will affect the blood.
explanation.definitionFit: This fatty substance carried in the bloodstream raises the risk of clogged arteries when its level is high.

clue.text: Except when climbing into vehicle, continuing with financial irregularity

indicators.note: into says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a taxi is a vehicle for hire

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word is read upwards, backwards

explanation.walkthrough: 'when climbing' turns SAVE into EVAS, which goes 'into' TAXI, followed by ON.

clue.text: Stone whence bird ascends having eaten headless beast

explanation.definitionFit: The Koh-i-Noor is a famous Indian diamond among the British Crown Jewels, a precious stone.

clue.text: Home student in game is probably going to wonder

parts.note: chess is a board game
in means at home
L is a learner, so a student

explanation.surface: A student staying at home during a game is likely to start pondering.

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective so often precedes that noun in the set phrase for a weak-willed toff that it is likely to come next.

clue.text: Low-lying feature of 2 — judge is about right in case

clue.text: Deaf characters find a road, as old soldiers do

clue.text: Sky pilot's abuse of rod — there's a lot of it about

clue.text: Gives birth almost without trouble, which calls for a drink
